questions.question_text:
The passage given below talks about the depletion of natural resources. However, some of the important words, phrases, and expressions have been omitted. Complete the passage by filling-in all the blanks choosing from the options provided for each blank:

The Passage
We often talk of the depleting natural resources_____(1.1)__________us. One common worry is about the availability of potable water in not so distant a future. Every summer, a large number of villages and cities in our country are reported to be reeling under acute shortage water. It seems that suddenly the age-old rivers, well, and ponds are drying _____(1.2)_____ and the fertile lands have become barren overnight. However, if we observe closely, it is not so. Well, it’s true that all of this is happening, but hasn’t happened just in a couple of days, months, or years. ______(1.3)___________ several decades now, we have not just used, but also overused, and even exploited natural resources without any sense of remorse, concern, care, or guilt. It seems we have become devoid _______(1.4)______________ such finer sentiments.

SubQuestion No : 1
With reference to the passage, select the word that you think best fits the blank 1.1
questions.explanation: In the context of natural resources existing in our environment, the preposition 'around' is the most appropriate to describe resources surrounding us.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the passage in Question ID 582113248. 

SubQuestion No : 2
With reference to the passage, select the word that you think best fits the blank 1.2
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'drying up' is the standard English expression used to describe the disappearance of water from rivers or ponds.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the passage in Question ID 582113248.

SubQuestion No : 3
With reference to the passage, select the word that you think best fits the blank 1.3
questions.explanation: The preposition 'For' is used to denote a period of time (several decades) extending up to the present in the context of the present perfect tense.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the passage in Question ID 582113248. 

SubQuestion No : 4
With reference to the passage, select the word that you think best fits the blank 1.4
questions.explanation: The adjective 'devoid' is consistently followed by the preposition 'of' to mean lacking or free from something.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements is appropriate in terms of grammar and usage?

options.A: The foreign delegation comprising of many experts is likely to visit our university next week.
options.B: The foreign delegation comprising many experts is likely to visit our university next week.
options.C: The foreign delegation comprising many experts are likely to visit our university next week.
options.D: The foreign delegation comprising of many experts are likely to visit our university next week.

questions.explanation: The verb 'comprise' does not take the preposition 'of' in the active voice. Additionally, 'delegation' is a collective noun acting as a singular subject, requiring the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question_text: Which is of the following statements is appropriate in terms of grammar and usage?

options.A: Sir, I passed my B.Tech in 2024.
options.B: Sir, I had passed my B.Tech in 2024.
options.C: Sir, I have passed my B.Tech in 2024.
options.D: Sir, I have been passed my B.Tech in 2024.

questions.explanation: When a specific time in the past is mentioned (2024), the simple past tense ('passed') is the grammatically correct choice.

questions.question_text:
Which of the expressions given below will appropriately fill-in the blank in the following statement?
_________________________________we have decided to give this matter an open hearing.

options.A: In view of you have been raising this issue for quite some time now,
options.B: However, you have raised this issue for quite some time now, therefore,
options.C: Regardless of you have always been raising this issue for quite some time now,
options.D: Since you have been raising this issue for quite some time now,

questions.explanation: 'Since' acts as a subordinating conjunction introducing a reason, making the sentence logically and grammatically complete.

questions.question_text: _________________________________we have decided to give this matter an open hearing.

questions.question_text:
Choose the most appropriate word from the given options to correctly complete the following sentence:
He was such a ________________ man! He believed whatever anyone said.

questions.question_text:
Choose the most appropriate word from the given options to correctly complete the following sentence:
Despite all claims to equality, a woman’s career and position in our society often remains ____________________ and stunted.

Comprehension:
Caselet 1: Rising Employee Absenteeism at Oasis Electronics
Read the caselet given below and answer the questions that follow:
Oasis Electronics, a medium-sized manufacturing company, began experiencing a steady rise in employee absenteeism over six months. Production schedules were frequently disrupted, deadlines were missed, and supervisors struggled to redistribute workloads among present staff. Initial reviews showed that absences were highest in departments with repetitive tasks, timings which were rigidly imposed, and communication limited between managers and workers. Employees reported feeling undervalued, physically exhausted, and unclear about performance expectations. Although the company introduced stricter attendance policies, but absenteeism continued, suggesting that punitive measures alone were ineffective. Management latter realized that poor workplace communication, lack of flexibility, and minimal recognition were key contributors to the problem. Addressing absenteeism, however, required enforcing not just rules but also improving engagement, clarifying roles, and creating a supportive work environment. The case highlights how language, tone, and clarity in expression in internal communication can influence employee behavior as much as formal policies.

SubQuestion No : 11
The phrase punitive measures refers to the actions that are
questions.explanation: Punitive measures are actions taken as punishment for an offense, intended to correct behavior through disciplinary consequences.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113259.

SubQuestion No : 12
The expression in the caselet, ‘’repetitive tasks, timings which were rigidly imposed, and communication limited,’’ lacks parallel grammatical structure. Which of following constructions would make the structure parallel?

options.A: Tasks repetitive, rigid shift timings, limited communication
options.B: Timings strictly imposed, tasks demanded repetitively, and limited communication
options.C: Repetitive tasks, shifts that are rigid, communication limited
options.D: Repetitive tasks, rigid shift timings, and limited communication

questions.explanation: Parallelism requires items in a list to follow the same grammatical form. Option D uses the consistent pattern of 'Adjective + Noun'.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113259.

SubQuestion No : 13
There is an error in the expression: ‘’Although the company introduced stricter attendance policies, but absenteeism continued suggesting that punitive measures alone were ineffective.’’ Choose the right option to render the sentence grammatically appropriate.

options.A: Delete ‘Although’ from the main clause and replace it with ‘However’

questions.explanation: The conjunctions 'Although' and 'but' are redundant when used together in the same sentence; 'Although' already establishes the contrast.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113259.

SubQuestion No : 14
In the expression, ‘’…began experiencing a steady rise in employee absenteeism…’’ the word ‘experiencing’ has been used as a:
questions.explanation: In this context, 'experiencing' acts as a noun (the object of the verb 'began'), making it a gerund.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113259.

SubQuestion No : 15
There is an error in the expression, ‘’Management latter realized…’’ Which of the following options would make it grammatically appropriate?
questions.explanation: The word 'latter' refers to the second of two things, whereas 'later' is the adverb of time required to indicate a subsequent realization.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113259.

SubQuestion No : 16
The expression: ‘’Addressing absenteeism, therefore, required enforcing not just rules improved engagement as well…’’ is grammatically faulty. Which of the following options would make the sentence grammatically appropriate?

options.A: Addressing absenteeism, therefore, required not only enforcing rules but also improving engagement
options.B: Addressing absenteeism, therefore, required not just enforcing rules but also improving engagement
options.C: Addressing absenteeism, thus, required not only to enforce rules but also improved employee engagement
options.D: Addressing absenteeism, therefore, required not only rules but also improvement in employee engagement

questions.explanation: The correlative conjunction 'not only... but also' correctly connects two parallel phrases ('enforcing rules' and 'improving engagement').

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113259.

SubQuestion No : 17
Take a look at the ending of the caselet again – ‘’The case highlights how language, tone, and clarity in expression in internal communication can influence employee behavior as much as formal policies.’’ Now identify the words/expressions that are redundant in this statement.

options.C: …can influence employee behaviour as much as formal policies.

questions.explanation: The phrase 'in expression in internal communication' is redundant because the preceding words 'language, tone, and clarity' already imply the mode of expression.

questions.question_text:
Comprehension:
Caselet 2: Lustre Beauty Line and Strategic Brand Communication
Go through the caselet given below and answer the questions that follow:
It was in 2024 that Lustre Beauty Line, a mid-sized skincare, brand has entered a crowded market dominated by global giants and local herbal labels. To stand out, the company positioned itself as “science backed yet gentle emissary,” that thrive on combining clinical testing with natural ingredients. It’s marketing campaigned focused on social media influencers, short video tutorials, and customer testimonials rather than traditional advertising. The brand’s language was carefully chosen—simple, reassuring, and aspirational—to appeal to young, urban consumers who valued authenticity. Lustre Beauty Line avoided exaggerated claims, instead highlighting transparency in sourcing and visible results over time. However, critics argued that the campaign relied too heavily on buzzwords like clean, pure, and natural, which were vague and overused. Despite this, consistent messaging, parallel slogans, and visually appealing packaging helped Lustre Beauty Line building trust. Within no time, the brand achieved strong recall and loyalty, proving that thoughtful communication and precise language can shape perception as powerfully as the product itself.

SubQuestion No : 18
The opening line in the caselet – ‘’It was in 2024 that Lustre Beauty Line, a mid-sized skincare, brand has entered a crowded market…’’ is grammatically inconsistent. Which of the following statements would render it grammatically appropriate?

options.A: It was in 2024 that Lustre Beauty Line, a mid-sized skincare, brand had entered a crowded market
options.B: It was in 2024 that Lustre Beauty Line a mid-sized skincare brand has entered a crowded market
options.C: It was in 2024 that Lustre Beauty Line, a mid-sized skincare, brand would have entered a crowded market
options.D: It was in 2024 that Lustre Beauty Line, a mid-sized skincare brand, entered a crowded market

questions.explanation: When referencing a specific past year (2024), the simple past tense ('entered') is required instead of the present perfect ('has entered').

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113267.

SubQuestion No : 19
The word “emissary” in the expression “science-backed yet gentle emissary” can be replaced with which of the following words?
questions.explanation: 'Envoy' is a synonym for 'emissary', both referring to a representative or messenger sent on a mission.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113267.

SubQuestion No : 20
The expression - “that thrive on combining clinical testing with natural ingredients,” is grammatically inconsistent. Which of the following statements would make it grammatically appropriate?

options.A: That throve on combined clinical testing and natural ingredients
options.B: That thrived on combined clinical tests with natural ingredients
options.C: That thrives on combining clinical testing with natural ingredients
options.D: That thrive on clinical testing as well as natural ingredient

questions.explanation: The subject 'emissary' is singular, therefore the verb must also be singular ('thrives') to maintain subject-verb agreement.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113267.

SubQuestion No : 21
What is the best way to rewrite the statement, “It’s marketing campaigned focussed on social media influencers, short video tutorials, and customer testimonials…”

options.A: Its marketing campaigners focussed on social media influencers, short video tutorials and customer testimonials…
options.B: It’s marketing campaigning focussed on social media influencers, short video tutorials and customer testimonials…
options.C: Its’ marketing campaign focussed on social media influencers, short video tutorials and customer testimonials…
options.D: Its marketing campaign focussed on social media influencers, short video tutorials, and customer testimonials…

questions.explanation: 'Its' is the correct possessive pronoun. 'It's' is a contraction for 'it is'. Additionally, 'campaign' is the appropriate noun form for the marketing effort.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113267.

SubQuestion No : 22
The structure of the phrase – “the campaign relied too heavily on buzzwords…” is:

options.A: the (article); campaign (noun); relied (verb); too (adverb); heavily (adverb); on (preposition); buzzwords (noun)
options.B: the (article); campaign (noun); relied (verb); too (adjective); heavily (adverb); on (preposition); buzzwords (conjunction)
options.C: the (article); campaign (noun); relied (verb); too (conjunction); heavily (adverb); on (preposition); buzzwords (relative pronoun)
options.D: the (article); campaign (noun); relied (verb); too (adverb); heavily (adjective); on (preposition); buzzwords (noun)

questions.explanation: This breakdown correctly identifies the word classes: 'too' modifies the adverb 'heavily', thus both are adverbs.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113267.

SubQuestion No : 23
The expression, “…and visually appealing packaging helped Lustre Beauty Line building trust,” can be rendered grammatically appropriate by replacing it with:

options.A: …and visually appealing packaging helped Lustre Beauty Line to build up trust
options.B: …and visually appealing packaging helped Lustre Beauty Line builds trust
options.C: …and visually appealing packaging helped Lustre Beauty Line build trust
options.D: …and visually appealing packaging helped Lustre Beauty Line building up trust

questions.explanation: The verb 'help' can be followed by a bare infinitive ('build') or a 'to-infinitive', but not by a gerund ('building') in this context.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113267.

SubQuestion No : 24
Which modifier placement is most effective in a professional context?

options.A: The brand chose its carefully language.
options.B: Carefully, the brand chose its language
options.C: The brand carefully chose its language.
options.D: The brand chose carefully its language.

questions.explanation: Placing the adverb 'carefully' directly before the verb it modifies ('chose') provides the most clarity and formal flow in professional writing.

Refer to the caselet in Question ID 582113267.

SubQuestion No : 25
Which of the following figures of speech would be an apt descriptor for the phrase, “global giants” in the caselet?
questions.explanation: “Global giants” is a metaphor because it compares large companies to giants to emphasize their scale and power without using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.question_text:
Read the paragraph given below and choose from the options given underneath what you think would be the most appropriate introducer and can serve as an opening statement:

Their job, however, is not all that easy as it seems. It is so because the customers’ aspirations, and hence their preference for a certain product, may stem from difference in age, sex, income, or culture of the customer. Therefore, the promoters and advertising agencies have a lot to study and thinking to do before deciding on choosing a captivating image, an intriguing but hummable catch-line, an engaging video, couple of racy dialogues, and tuneful jingle accompanying a product that they wish to promote among a certain segment of potential customers.

options.A: Advertisers know that young girls might prefer watching advertisements related to beauty products while young boys may choose a product endorsed by a famous cricketer.
options.B: Riding the crest of raging consumerism, advertisements continue to play with the desires, emotions and ambitions of potential customers.
options.C: Advertising is probably the most interesting aspect of any entrepreneurial enterprise.
options.D: Advertisers are intelligent enough to know that old people cannot be lured with promises of swanky bikes.

questions.explanation: Option B provides a broad context about the role of advertisements in consumerism, which effectively introduces the subsequent discussion about the challenges advertisers face.

questions.question_text:
Comprehension:
Read the paragraph given below and answer the questions that follow:

It was such a beautiful feeling, so ennobling, so liberating! Something that I had cherished forever, dreamt forever, craved forever, was finally here. And it caused numbness in me, so I could not say anything even though I wanted to say a lot. Emotions floated to the brim inside me, but words required to convey them deserted me. Valiantly, I groped for the right words to express what I was going through, but it wasn’t possible. All of a sudden, speechlessness had descended on me as Rio stood in front of me on its four legs. Its two little eyes evoked compassion; its tail wagged perpetually announcing its love for all. Finally, when senses were revived in me, I hugged Daddy in unspeakable joy and gratitude. My best birthday gift ever had arrived and it had brought with it exquisite moment of love, happiness, and pride!

SubQuestion No : 32
The style of the paragraph appears to be:
questions.explanation: The paragraph tells a personal story using 'I' and 'me' to recount an emotional sequence of events, which characterizes the narrative style.

questions.question_text:
Refer to the paragraph in Question ID 582113283.

SubQuestion No : 33
As used in the passage, which of the following expressions will not be a synonym of the word perpetually?
questions.explanation: 'Perpetually' means never-ending or constant. 'Occasionally' refers to something that happens only sometimes, making it an antonym, not a synonym.
